authority.abi: C ABI unchanged; no export, signature, #[repr(C)] layout or CRYPTO_* seam coordinate changed
external_contracts: All entry points are unsafe extern "C" or safe functions over private Rust state; no safe Rust caller can reach an unchecked raw operation.

The process-global registries (OBJ_NAME, X509_VERIFY_PARAM) must not be cleaned up concurrently with a live lookup that is still using a returned borrowed pointer (authority documents these as not thread safe).
A BIO callback must not free or otherwise invalidate the BIO while a dispatch operation is in progress.
The OBJ_NAME per-type cmp/hash callbacks must be pure; they run under the registry mutex, as in the authority.
Default-table rows are const objects; a caller must not const-cast and write them.

residuals: Zero-state destructor correctness rests on the established CtxDestroy obligation (all releases NULL-tolerant); exercised by zero_state_sweep_file_ctx_st.
The object callback is the store's internal ossl_store_handle_load_result, not application code; application post-process/passphrase callbacks run outside this unit under OSSL_STORE_load's contract.
OSSL_STORE_load must not be re-entered via OSSL_STORE_close from a callback; authority-wide external precondition.

boundaries.mechanism: URI/path parsing and fixed two-slot path array
residuals: X509_NAME_oneline may return NULL on allocation failure and is passed to BIO_snprintf "%s"; glibc prints "(null)", authority-inherited, not Rust UB.
The pre-call passes processed = NULL; the legacy branch dereferences it only on the RETURN leg, and the modern callback contract admits NULL on the pre-call.

boundaries.mechanism: BIO field access across method and callback edges

defects.description: Each dispatch function formed let b = &mut *bio and then touched the same allocation through the raw bio pointer (has_callback, the method call, the callback) before using b again (init/num_read/num_write). Under Stacked/Tree Borrows the parent raw access invalidates the live &mut, so the later field access is UB.
defects.repair: Removed the long-lived &mut; method/init/counter fields are re-read or written through the raw pointer with a SAFETY contract, matching the file's existing BIO_get_line pattern. No ABI or behaviour change.

residuals: A callback that frees or invalidates the BIO mid-operation is outside the callback contract; the dispatch layer re-reads fields but cannot make a freed allocation live.

boundaries.mechanism: dynamic ASN1_OBJECT database (OBJ_DB) and NID counter
residuals: alloc_oid_object narrows data.len() to c_int; the ASN.1 OID content is bounded by the caller's string, and the authority's length field is int, so the truncation is not reachable through the decoder's accepted OID sizes.

boundaries.mechanism: OBJ_NAME registry: add/get/remove/new_index/cleanup; per-type destructor and comparator

defects.description: The caller-registered free_func ran while the registry mutex was held. A destructor that re-enters the registry deadlocks; the authority also runs it under its lock.
defects.repair: Destructors are resolved when the record leaves the registry and are run after the lock is dropped (or deferred to the end of a live walk).

residuals: A user cmp callback runs under the registry mutex (authority parity). The callback must be pure; re-entry that needs the same mutex deadlocks. No production type registers a custom comparator or hash.

boundaries.mechanism: OBJ_NAME_do_all / do_all_sorted iteration and borrowed pointers

defects.description: The walk snapshotted NameRec and released the lock before calling the visitor. A callback that removed/replaced another entry ran that entry's destructor, freeing the name/data pointers still held by the snapshot; the authority instead holds its read lock across the walk (and would deadlock rather than hand out freed pointers).
defects.repair: Snapshot + active_walks counter + deferred destructor list, released by a RAII WalkGuard at the end of the last live walk (including on unwind). The lock is never held across a callback, a callback may re-enter the registry, and snapshot pointers stay valid because destruction is deferred.
defects.divergence: Destructor timing is deferred to the end of the walk instead of running inside it; observable only through allocator-hook timing. Authority behaviour on re-entrant mutation is a deadlock, so this is a deliberate safety improvement.

defects.severity: high (self-deadlock; regression introduced and removed within this batch)
defects.description: Holding the registry read lock across the visitor deadlocks against the production callback context::namemap::prepopulate_legacy_names, whose get_legacy_* visitors call OBJ_NAME_get (nested read) while concurrent first-use initialization queues a writer.
defects.repair: The snapshot + deferred-destructor design above holds no lock across the visitor.

residuals: OBJ_NAME_get returns a borrowed data pointer after unlocking; a concurrent remove/cleanup may free it before the caller uses it (authority contract: the caller keeps the entry alive).
Deferred frees are pinned until the last walk ends; a long-running walk can delay allocator-observable release.

defects.description: The table was wrapped in UnsafeCell while documented as write-once/read-only, advertising interior mutability the authority's static const does not have.
defects.repair: Removed UnsafeCell; the table is a plain static accessed through addr_of! and *const, so a const-cast write faults instead of silently mutating shared verifier state.

residuals: A C caller that casts get0/lookup to mutable and writes a default row is outside the authority's const contract.

defects.description: The table pointer was an AtomicPtr but the stack it names was sorted, searched, mutated and freed without any lock. Concurrent first-use/verification was a data race, and table_cleanup could free a stack another thread had just loaded.
defects.repair: The slot and every stack operation are serialised by a Mutex<ParamTable>; the pointer is never dereferenced outside the guard. Releases that can reach a caller allocator hook run after the guard is dropped.

residuals: get0/lookup return pointers into the table after unlocking; table_cleanup must not race a live use (authority documents these entry points as not thread safe). External precondition.

boundaries.mechanism: table add0/lookup/get0 ownership and null-key guards

defects.description: id < 0 computed default_table_ptr().add(id as usize), forming a pointer before the static array; UB even without a read.
A NULL lookup key or an unnamed param reached param_cmp/strcmp(NULL, ...).
defects.repair: lookup(NULL) returns NULL; add0_table refuses NULL and unnamed params without transferring ownership.

residuals: add0_table still consumes a NID on OBJ_create's collision path (authority parity).

negative_controls.control: cargo test --lib bn::blinding:: -- --test-threads=4 against the intermediate read-lock design: EXIT=124 (hang); against the final design: EXIT=0, 11 passed. The defect class fired before the repair.
name_do_all_admits_reentry_and_defers_removal: nested OBJ_NAME_get succeeds, nested remove returns 1, destructor count is 0 during the walk, 1 at walk end, 2 after cleanup.
name_destructor_runs_outside_the_registry_lock: try_lock succeeds at destructor time and a re-entrant read succeeds; a reintroduced lock fails the assertion instead of hanging.

eliminated: eight long-lived &mut Bio borrows spanning callbacks/method calls (B1-BIO-2)
unsynchronised raw stack mutation through AtomicPtr<OpenSslStack> (B1-VPM-2)
UnsafeCell interior mutability over the const default table (B1-VPM-1)
out-of-bounds pointer formation for negative table ids (B1-VPM-3)
relocated: raw BIO field reads/writes now each carry an explicit validity contract (same raw pointer, no long-lived reference)
registry mutation and iteration serialised by short-lived mutex guards; release outside the guard
table slot + stack operations serialised by one mutex
new_obligations: OBJ_NAME do_all visitors may read and mutate the registry; removals are deferred and destructor timing moves to walk end
PARAM_TABLE/get0/lookup callers must not race table_cleanup (external, authority parity)
